enzyme_name: talamine 3-N-methyltransferase (SAM-dependent N-methyltransferase of the hygromycin B / hygromycin C aminoglycoside pathway)
organism_context: Streptomyces hygroscopicus (hygromycin B/C, destomycin-family pseudodisaccharide biosynthesis)
rationale: Local MetaCyc dump places RXN-23145 in the hygromycin C branch (talamine/galacamine -> 3-N-methyltalamine/3-N-methylgalacamine -> hygromycin C, CPD-25583), so the catalyst is a cluster-encoded SAM N-methyltransferase, but I could not pin the gene product in the literature and so will not assert its domain content.
direction_note: SAM-dependent N-methylation with SAH release is effectively irreversible; ModelSEED's reverse-only call would make SAH + 3-N-methyltalamine regenerate SAM, which no methyltransferase does.

enzyme_name: salicylic-acid-binding protein 2 / methyl salicylate esterase (SABP2, MES-family alpha/beta hydrolase) acting on acibenzolar-S-methyl
organism_context: Nicotiana tabacum SABP2 and orthologues in citrus and potato; the plant target of the SAR activator acibenzolar-S-methyl (ASM/Actigard)
rationale: Tripathi et al. showed SABP2, the tobacco methyl salicylate esterase, is required for ASM-induced SAR because it de-esterifies ASM to the free acibenzolar acid, which is exactly this reaction. SABP2 carries a single Ser-His-Asp esterase site; its reported 'lipase' activity is the same hydrolase chemistry on a different ester, i.e. promiscuity, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: Carboxylic/thioester hydrolysis in bulk water is irreversible; ModelSEED's reverse-only call would have free methanol re-esterify the thioacid, which an esterase cannot do without an activated acyl donor.

enzyme_name: broad-specificity flavonoid 7-O-beta-D-glucosidase (beta-glucosidase, MetaCyc EC 3.2.1.62)
rationale: MetaCyc RXN-22892 carries only the generic EC 3.2.1.62 shared across a whole block of flavonoid 7-O-glucoside hydrolyses it curates together (luteolin-, apigenin-, chrysoeriol-7-O-glucoside, ononin), so no specific protein is identified and I will not guess its domain content.
direction_note: Glycoside hydrolysis is strongly exergonic and irreversible; ModelSEED's reverse-only call would have free D-glucose plus eriodictyol condense to the 7-O-glucoside, which requires UDP-glucose and a glycosyltransferase, not a glycosidase.

enzyme_name: phospholipid-hydroperoxide glutathione peroxidase (GPX4 / PHGPx, EC 1.11.1.12)
organism_context: mammalian GPX4 and its plant/fungal PHGPx homologues; MetaCyc assigns EC 1.11.1.12 to this and the five sibling fatty-acid-hydroperoxide reductions in this chunk
rationale: A single selenocysteine (or Cys) peroxidatic site reduces the 9(S)-hydroperoxide of linoleate to 9(S)-HODE at the expense of 2 GSH; GPX4's well-known second role as a structural component of the sperm mitochondrial capsule is structural moonlighting, explicitly not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: GSSG was dropped from the ModelSEED products (status MI:C:-20/H:-26/N:-6/O:-12/S:-2 = oxidized glutathione), which is what produces the nonsensical +381 kJ/mol group-contribution value driving the '<' call; peroxide O-O reduction by thiol is irreversible.

enzyme_name: beta-lactamase (penicillinase, EC 3.5.2.6)
organism_context: ubiquitous in Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria; serine (classes A/C/D) and metallo (class B) enzymes alike
rationale: The product is ampicilloate, the ring-opened penicilloic acid of ampicillin, i.e. the canonical beta-lactamase hydrolysis product; beta-lactamases carry one hydrolase active site. Called from established enzymology, not from a new search; note that the bifunctional transglycosylase/transpeptidase PBPs are a different protein family and are not the catalyst here.
direction_note: Beta-lactam ring opening relieves substantial four-membered-ring amide strain and is irreversible; ModelSEED's reverse-only call would have the open penicilloate spontaneously re-close to ampicillin and expel water.

enzyme_name: phospholipid-hydroperoxide glutathione peroxidase (GPX4 / PHGPx, EC 1.11.1.12)
organism_context: mammalian GPX4 and plant/fungal PHGPx homologues; 13(S)-HPODE is the major lipoxygenase product reduced by this enzyme
rationale: One peroxidatic selenocysteine site reduces 13(S)-HPODE to 13(S)-HODE using 2 GSH; the sperm-capsule structural role of GPX4 is moonlighting, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: GSSG is missing from the ModelSEED products (status MI:C:-20/H:-26/N:-6/O:-12/S:-2), inflating the group-contribution dG to +381 kJ/mol and manufacturing the '<' recommendation.

enzyme_name: none - uncatalysed hydrolysis of the imine intermediate of fructosamine oxidase (amadoriase, EC 1.5.3.26)
rationale: In the local MetaCyc dump RXN-22801 is the second half of the EC 1.5.3.26 reaction RXN-22795 (fructosyl-6-aminohexanoate + O2 + H2O -> fructosamine + 6-oxohexanoate + H2O2): RXN-22800 does the flavin oxidation to the imine and RXN-22801 hydrolyses it, carrying no EC of its own. No enzyme catalyses this step on its own.
direction_note: Schiff-base hydrolysis dominates in dilute water; ModelSEED's reverse-only call is the spontaneous condensation direction, which only matters at glycating sugar/amine concentrations.

enzyme_name: enterobacterial common antigen polymerase WzyE (Wzy-family polytopic inner-membrane polymerase)
organism_context: Escherichia coli, Shigella flexneri and other Enterobacteriaceae; acts on lipid III (Und-PP-GlcNAc-ManNAcA-Fuc4NAc)
rationale: MetaCyc RXN0-7383 is the ECA polymerase step, with enterobacterial common antigen (CPD-24126) as both acceptor and product; WzyE is a single polytopic membrane protein with one polymerisation (transglycosylation) activity, chain length being set by the separate WzzE co-polymerase rather than by a second WzyE domain.
direction_note: ModelSEED cancelled the generic ECA polymer that appears on both MetaCyc sides, leaving lipid III -> Und-PP with the whole trisaccharide repeat unit unaccounted for (status MI:C:-24/H:-34/N:-3/O:-15); the real step is irreversible biosynthetic polymerisation that releases Und-PP, i.e. the LLM orientation.

enzyme_name: phospholipid-hydroperoxide glutathione peroxidase (GPX4 / PHGPx, EC 1.11.1.12)
organism_context: mammalian GPX4; 12(S)-HpEPE is the 12-LOX hydroperoxide of eicosapentaenoate
rationale: Single peroxidatic selenocysteine site reducing 12(S)-HpEPE to 12(S)-HEPE with 2 GSH; the structural sperm-capsule role of GPX4 is moonlighting and does not make it bifunctional.
direction_note: GSSG missing from the products (status MI:C:-20/H:-26/N:-6/O:-12/S:-2) is what generates the +381/+188 kJ/mol estimates behind ModelSEED's '<'.

enzyme_name: tricarballylate dehydrogenase TcuA (FAD-dependent, acyl-CoA-dehydrogenase-like)
organism_context: Salmonella enterica sv. Typhimurium tcuABC operon; TcuB (4Fe-4S + heme) is a separate polypeptide that reoxidises TcuA's FADH2 to membrane acceptors
rationale: Lewis & Escalante-Semerena purified TcuA and showed the FAD-dependent oxidation of tricarballylate to cis-aconitate; the follow-up paper shows TcuB is a distinct protein handling electron egress, so TcuA is a monofunctional dehydrogenase, not a fused bifunctional enzyme.
direction_note: Free FAD/FADH2 stands in for TcuA-bound flavin drained by TcuB into the membrane quinone pool; with that sink removed the reaction looks near-equilibrium, which is what lets ModelSEED point it at aconitate reduction instead of the catabolic oxidation TcuA actually performs.

enzyme_name: xanthine dehydrogenase / xanthine oxidoreductase (XDH/XOR, molybdo-hydroxylase, EC 1.17.1.4)
organism_context: MetaCyc curates RXN-8754 in the xanthine-oxidoreductase purine hydroxylation series (purine -> 8-hydroxypurine/hypoxanthine -> 6,8-dihydroxypurine -> urate); eukaryotic XOR is a single chain, bacterial XdhABC is a multi-subunit complex
rationale: XOR's 2Fe-2S, FAD and molybdopterin domains support a single catalytic activity - Moco-dependent hydroxylation with water as the oxygen donor and electron egress through FAD - so the multidomain architecture is not bifunctionality; its aldehyde and NADH-oxidase side reactions use the same two sites.
direction_note: Molybdo-hydroxylase ring hydroxylation is physiologically unidirectional; ModelSEED's '<' would be reductive dehydroxylation of 6,8-dihydroxypurine by NADH, which XOR does not do.

enzyme_name: (pseudo)ephedrine N-methyltransferase (EsNMT, SAM-dependent amine N-methyltransferase)
organism_context: Ephedra sinica; EsNMT methylates norephedrine/norpseudoephedrine to ephedrine/pseudoephedrine and carries on to the N-methyl alkaloids
rationale: Morris et al. characterised EsNMT as the SAM-dependent N-methyltransferase of the Ephedra phenylalkylamine pathway, a single-domain class-I MTase; the second methylation giving (+)-N-methylpseudoephedrine is the same enzyme (or a close paralogue) acting again, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: SAM -> SAH methyl transfer is effectively irreversible; ModelSEED's reverse-only call would require SAH plus the N-methyl alkaloid to regenerate SAM.

enzyme_name: none identified - monothioarsenate hydrolysis is largely abiotic aqueous arsenic-sulfur speciation
organism_context: studied in alkaline sulfidic hot springs and in Thermocrinis ruber, which grows chemolithotrophically on monothioarsenate, but no protein has been assigned to this hydrolysis
rationale: MetaCyc RXN-22407 carries no EC and sits beside two other EC-less thioarsenate interconversions (RXN-22402, RXN-22404); monothioarsenate <-> arsenate + sulfide is pH- and sulfide-controlled solution chemistry, so no catalysing protein can be named.
direction_note: Both limbs are documented abiotically - hydrolysis to arsenate dominates at low pH, thiolation of arsenate by sulfide dominates in sulfide-rich water - so the direction is set by sulfide and pH, not by any enzyme.

enzyme_name: none - hydration of metaarsenite (AsO2-) to arsenite (H2AsO3-), an instantaneous aqueous speciation equilibrium
rationale: MetaCyc RXN-22312 has no EC and no partner reactions; AsO2- (CPD-24317, the solid-state/formal metaarsenite ion) and H2AsO3- (CPD-763) are two writings of the same dissolved As(III) species, so this entry records hydration chemistry rather than an enzyme.
direction_note: In water As(III) is fully hydrated to As(OH)3/H2AsO3-, so only the hydration limb occurs; ModelSEED's '<' would dehydrate arsenite in bulk water.

enzyme_name: phospholipid-hydroperoxide glutathione peroxidase (GPX4 / PHGPx, EC 1.11.1.12)
organism_context: mammalian GPX4; (15R)-HpETE is the aspirin-acetylated-COX-2 hydroperoxide reduced here to 15(R)-HETE
rationale: One peroxidatic selenocysteine site reduces (15R)-HpETE (C20H31O4) to 15(R)-HETE (C20H31O3) with 2 GSH - the substrate/product pair does correspond despite ModelSEED mislabelling the product '(15R)-hydroxyeicosapentaenoate'; GPX4's sperm-capsule role is structural moonlighting.
direction_note: GSSG dropped from the products (status MI:C:-20/H:-26/N:-6/O:-12/S:-2) is the sole source of the +381/+190 kJ/mol estimates behind the '<' recommendation.

enzyme_name: none - uncatalysed hydrolysis of the imine intermediate of fructosyl-amino-acid oxidase (amadoriase, EC 1.5.3.25)
rationale: The local MetaCyc dump has RXN-22793 as the complete EC 1.5.3.25 reaction (fructosyl-glutamine + O2 + H2O -> D-glucosone + Gln + H2O2) and RXN-22792 as its EC-less hydrolysis half; no enzyme catalyses this step by itself.
direction_note: Imine hydrolysis is the spontaneous direction in dilute water; ModelSEED's '<' is the glycation/condensation limb, which needs high sugar and amine pools.

enzyme_name: xanthine dehydrogenase / xanthine oxidoreductase (XDH/XOR, EC 1.17.1.4)
organism_context: MetaCyc RXN-8751 is C8 hydroxylation of hypoxanthine to 6,8-dihydroxypurine, part of the classical XOR purine-analogue hydroxylation series; single chain in eukaryotes, XdhABC complex in bacteria
rationale: A single Moco hydroxylase site does the chemistry, with the 2Fe-2S and FAD domains serving electron egress rather than a second catalytic activity; where XOR is a bacterial XdhABC complex the protocol's multi-subunit exclusion applies and the catalytic subunit is still monofunctional.
direction_note: MetaCyc writes RXN-8751 reversible, but molybdo-hydroxylase ring hydroxylation runs oxidatively in vivo; ModelSEED's '<' would be NADH-driven reductive dehydroxylation, which XOR does not perform.

enzyme_name: phospholipid-hydroperoxide glutathione peroxidase (GPX4 / PHGPx, EC 1.11.1.12)
organism_context: mammalian GPX4 in the specialised pro-resolving mediator branch: (7S,17S)-HHpDHA is reduced to resolvin D5
rationale: The 17-hydroperoxide of the DHA-derived intermediate is reduced to the 17-hydroxyl of RvD5 at GPX4's single peroxidatic selenocysteine using 2 GSH; the sperm-capsule role is structural moonlighting.
direction_note: GSSG was dropped from the products (status MI:C:-20/H:-26/N:-6/O:-12/S:-2); the missing oxidant sink is what makes the dG estimates nonsensical and flips the ModelSEED call.

enzyme_name: none - uncatalysed hydrolysis of the imine released by putrescine dehydrogenase/oxidase
rationale: MetaCyc pairs RXN-21436 with RXN-21435 (putrescine + NAD+ -> 4-iminobutan-1-amine + NADH), i.e. it is the EC-less hydrolysis half of the amine dehydrogenase reaction that yields 4-aminobutanal + ammonia; no enzyme is assigned to the hydrolysis.
direction_note: Hydrolysis of a protonated aldimine to aldehyde plus ammonia is strongly favoured in water; the +17 to +46 kJ/mol estimates driving ModelSEED's '<' are group-contribution artefacts for the imine group.

enzyme_name: phospholipid-hydroperoxide glutathione peroxidase (GPX4 / PHGPx, EC 1.11.1.12)
organism_context: mammalian GPX4 and plant PHGPx homologues; 9(S)-HPOTrE is the 9-LOX hydroperoxide of alpha-linolenate, prominent in plant oxylipin metabolism
rationale: A single peroxidatic selenocysteine (Cys in most plant PHGPx) reduces 9(S)-HPOTrE to 9-HOTrE with 2 GSH; no second catalytic activity on the chain.
direction_note: GSSG missing from the ModelSEED products (status MI:C:-20/H:-26/N:-6/O:-12/S:-2) manufactures the +381 kJ/mol value behind the '<' recommendation; thiol reduction of a peroxide is irreversible.

enzyme_name: aminodeoxychorismate synthase (ADCS; PabA glutamine amidotransferase + PabB ADC synthase, fused into one chain in plants and many bacteria)
organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana ADCS is a single bifunctional GAT-ADCS polypeptide (and apicomplexan parasites likewise); in Escherichia coli the two activities sit on separate PabA and PabB polypeptides, which would be a complex rather than a bifunctional enzyme
rationale: Camara et al. dissected the coupling between the glutamine amidotransferase and aminodeoxychorismate synthase domains of the single-chain Arabidopsis ADCS; the odd 2-Gln/1-free-NH3 stoichiometry MetaCyc records for RXN-22440 is exactly the partial uncoupling of those two domains.
direction_note: ModelSEED dropped the product 4-amino-4-deoxychorismate entirely (status MI:C:-10/H:-7/N:-1/O:-5), so the stored equation is glutamine hydrolysis with chorismate vanishing; the real reaction is driven irreversibly by amide hydrolysis in the GAT domain, i.e. the LLM orientation.

enzyme_name: none - uncatalysed hydrolysis of the imine intermediate of fructosyl-valine oxidase (amadoriase, EC 1.5.3.25)
rationale: MetaCyc holds both the full EC 1.5.3.25 reaction RXN-22787 (fructosyl-valine + O2 + H2O -> D-glucosone + Val + H2O2) and this EC-less hydrolysis half RXN-22789; the hydrolysis is spontaneous, so no enzyme can be named for it alone.
direction_note: Schiff-base hydrolysis is the spontaneous limb in dilute water; ModelSEED's '<' is the glycation condensation that only runs at high glucosone and amino-acid pools.

enzyme_name: succinate:plastoquinone oxidoreductase (complex II / succinate dehydrogenase, SdhA flavoprotein + SdhB iron-sulfur + membrane anchors, EC 1.3.5.1)
organism_context: oxygenic phototrophs (cyanobacteria/plastids), where succinate dehydrogenase feeds electrons into the plastoquinone pool shared with photosynthetic electron transport
rationale: The catalytic succinate oxidation happens at the covalent-FAD site of the SdhA polypeptide alone; SdhB and the membrane anchors that carry electrons to quinone are separate chains, so under the protocol's multi-subunit exclusion this is a complex of monofunctional subunits, not a fused bifunctional enzyme.
direction_note: SQR/QFR enzymes are intrinsically bidirectional and the direction is set by quinone-pool poise, but with plastoquinone (Em ~ +80 mV) above the fumarate/succinate couple (+30 mV) in an aerobic/phototrophic host the oxidative LLM direction is the physiological one, so ModelSEED's reverse-only lock is the worse call; the [0]/[1] compartment tags also make ModelSEED mislabel this membrane enzyme a transport reaction.

enzyme_name: putative anaerobic benzene carboxylase (AbcA/AbcD, UbiD/UbiX-family carboxylase; never purified)
organism_context: Fe(III)-reducing, nitrate-reducing and methanogenic benzene-degrading enrichment cultures; identified only by metagenomics/metatranscriptomics/proteomics of the consortium
rationale: Benzene carboxylation is the established anaerobic ring-activation step, but the activity has only ever been inferred from highly expressed UbiD-family gene clusters in enrichment cultures and proteomic detection - no protein has been isolated, so its subunit and domain content is genuinely unknown.
direction_note: UbiD-family (de)carboxylation is near-equilibrium here (all three dG estimators within ~3 kJ/mol of zero) and is reversible in principle, but in the organisms that own this reaction it runs as carboxylation, pulled by downstream benzoate-CoA ligase; ModelSEED's '<' would make these cultures produce benzene from benzoate.

enzyme_name: succinate:caldariellaquinone oxidoreductase (archaeal complex II, SdhABCD, EC 1.3.5.1)
organism_context: Sulfolobus/Saccharolobus and other Sulfolobales, whose respiratory chain uses caldariellaquinone (Em ~ +100 mV) in place of ubiquinone
rationale: Succinate oxidation occurs at the flavoprotein SdhA subunit; the iron-sulfur and membrane subunits that pass electrons to caldariellaquinone are separate polypeptides, so the protocol's multi-subunit exclusion makes the catalytic subunit monofunctional rather than the complex bifunctional.
direction_note: The SQR/QFR family is bidirectional and poised by the quinone pool, but Sulfolobales are obligate aerobes whose complex II runs succinate oxidation into caldariellaquinone, so ModelSEED's fumarate-reductase-only lock is wrong; the [0]/[1] compartment tags also make ModelSEED treat this membrane enzyme as a transport reaction.
